author: Mark Atwood
text:
Rust idiom confidence (5th rusty pass, 2026-05-17): ~10% chance of missed issue. Lower than the 4th rusty pass's 12% because (a) the scope was deliberately narrowed to new code introduced by the 28 commits between 2026-05-16 and 2026-05-17, which is a bounded surface to audit; (b) the dead-suppression finding (.105) is mechanical and verifiable — three independent clippy invocations all confirm the lint does not fire, so the engineering basis is fact rather than judgment; (c) the canonical-template divergence finding (.104) was confirmed by direct grep of 26 chat-server sites vs 48 mail-server sites with byte-different shape.

Least confident flags:
- .104 (args.remove canonical-template divergence) — engineering basis stands as a propagation finding, but the chat-server form is harmless behaviorally; a reviewer could argue mail-server's shape is itself just a different convention rather than a canonical one, and the divergence is policy not idiom. Held at P2 because the propagation rule in workspace AGENTS.md is explicit.
- .106 (find_map vs if-let chain) — pre-emptively held P3 because the engineering basis is local readability, not soundness or maintainability across the workspace. A reviewer who weights step-debugger ergonomics higher than combinator-chain expressiveness could downgrade to opinion.

Uncertainty driven by:
(1) clippy::pedantic was run -p jmap-chat-server only, not --workspace. The .54/.56/.89/.90 workspace-pervasive question (raised in 2nd-pass and reaffirmed in 4th-pass confidence notes) is still open. Same gap as the 4th pass.

(2) cargo doc was NOT rendered (writes target/doc/, forbidden by read-only rule). Same gap as the 4th pass.

(3) integration.rs sample was scoped to grep-only — magic-string ids and helper-duplication patterns from prior passes (.81/.82) are unchanged surface; this pass did not look for new test-code patterns introduced by the 28 commits' test additions (the Space/join 6-test module in space.rs, the apply_space_patch direct-call cap tests).

(4) NO custom ChatBackend was compiled against the rustdoc-only contract. Same gap as every prior pass. The new commit ceda248 introduced builder setters on OpResult (with_op_index, with_outcome) that look idiomatic by inspection but a real consumer compiling against them would surface contract-shape friction that a mental walk does not.

(5) The 28 commits include 5 BREAKING-CHANGE-marked refactors (chat-types Message::new 13→9 args, expire_message Result tightening, may_set_custom_emoji SetError-on-deny, patch_map→SpaceMetadataPatch, ChatBackend sync-vs-async carve-up). These are workspace-API-shape changes that a workspace-API supplement (review-workspace-api) would audit. The rusty pass only verified the local idiom of each change; it did NOT assess whether the workspace-API surface in aggregate is more or less idiomatic post-changes.

Would raise confidence to ~5% if:
(a) clippy::pedantic was swept workspace-wide so the .54/.56/.89/.90/.104/.105 propagation questions resolve in one pass across all 30 sibling crates;
(b) cargo doc was rendered (non-read-only pass) and the HTML inspected;
(c) integration.rs new test code (Space/join idempotent tests, apply_space_patch direct-call tests) was sampled for the same patterns as .81/.82/.83;
(d) a workspace-API supplement on the 5 breaking changes from this commit window confirms idiom consistency post-refactor.

At this point the diminishing-returns curve is very steep. A 6th rusty pass would likely produce 0-1 findings, all opinion or workspace-canonical-propagation of patterns already filed. The rusty review has converged on chat-server. Further investment goes to (1) fixing the 6 open findings from this pass + .85/.87 workspace canonicals; (2) the workspace-API supplement on the 5 breaking changes; (3) propagating the args.remove-shape and the dead-suppression-sweep to chat-server in one cleanup pass.
